description: Search everywhere and in a hurry!

latest_release.name: v6.1.0
latest_release.body:
## Security

- **Includes the `sort_link` / `sort_url` fix released as 6.0.1.** Request params were passed to `url_for`, so a crafted query string such as `?script_name=javascript:...` made sort links run script in the app's origin or point to another site (reflected XSS and open redirect). Ransack now drops `url_for`'s URL options (`script_name`, `host`, `protocol`, `only_path`, ...) from the params it carries into the link. GHSA-58rx-96gf-w92x.

## Compatibility

- **Ruby 3.3 or later and Rails 8.1 or later are required.** Ruby 3.2 reached end of life on 2026-03-31, Rails 7.2 on 2026-08-09 and Rails 8.0 on 2026-11-07; none of them receives security fixes. Nothing else changes, so on a supported Ruby and Rails the upgrade needs no code changes. On Ruby 3.2 or Rails 8.0 or earlier, stay on 6.0. — #1756, #1786

## Features

- **`add_predicate` takes `arel_node:`**, a callable that receives the attribute and the cast value and returns a finished Arel node, so a custom predicate can combine conditions without monkey patching `Arel::Predications`:

  ```ruby
  config.add_predicate 'gteq_or_null',
    arel_node: ->(attr, val) { attr.gteq(val).or(attr.eq(nil)) }
  ```

  It can't be combined with `arel_predicate`, has no `_any` / `_all` forms, and must return an `Arel::Nodes::Node` (anything else raises `ArgumentError`). The result is normalized like a built-in predicate's, and works with `null_sentinel`. — #1789 by @agrberg

## Bug fixes

Negative predicates on a collection (`articles_title_not_eq`, `tags_name_not_in`, `notes_note_not_cont`, ...) are built as a correlated subquery. 6.1 fixes how that subquery is built and which joins come with it:

- **Calling `result` twice, or putting two negative conditions on the same collection, no longer raises `NoMethodError`** (`undefined method 'table' for nil`). This was a regression in 6.0.0: `search.result` followed by `search.result.order_values`, a pair of conditions like `articles_title_not_eq` plus `articles_body_not_cont`, or an `_or_` attribute all failed. — #1746, fixes #1745
- **The subquery reaches the same records the association does.** It used to keep only the foreign-key correlation and drop the rest of the join, so it counted rows the association doesn't reach, and returned wrong records without raising:
  - the type column of a polymorphic `has_many ... as:`: a note on another model with the same id excluded the record
  - the target's default scope: a comment hidden by `default_scope` still excluded the record
  - the STI type column and the association's own scope
  - an association with a `primary_key:` option produced invalid SQL; it's now tested on that column

  — #1751, fixes #1747
- **A join something else in the search reads is kept.** A sort on the same collection (`s: 'articles_title asc'`, e.g. from a `sort_link`), or a condition or sort on an association nested under it (`articles_comments_body_eq`), referenced a join the negative condition had dropped (`no such column`). The join now stays alongside the subquery. — #1752, fixes #1749
- **A search can be changed after `result` and evaluated again.** Evaluating a search no longer changes it. A sort or condition added afterwards used to reference a dropped join, or an alias (`articles_people`) the query didn't have. The joins come from the search as it stands when it is evaluated, so clearing a sort or condition also drops its join instead of leaving one behind to repeat records. — #1753, fixes #1750
- **Every collection on the model gets the subquery.** It was only built when the attribute name started with the collection's table name, so an STI subclass (`story_articles_title_not_eq`), a scoped association (`published_articles_title_not_eq`) or one named differently from its table fell back to a join with a row-level `!=`, and returned records that do have a matching row. — #1783, fixes #1773

detail.readme: # Ransack > Search everywhere and in a hurry! [![Build Status](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/workflows/test/badge.svg)](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/actions) [![Gem Version](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ransack.svg)](http://badge.fury.io/rb/ransack) Ransack adds **searching and sorting to your Rails application** with plain Ruby and ERB, without a search server or any other infrastructure. Ransack is supported for Rails 8.1 on Ruby 3.4 and later, on Postgres, MySQL, Trilogy and SQLite. ```ruby gem 'ransack' ``` ```ruby @q = Post.ransack(params[:q]) @posts = @q.result ``` ```erb <%= search_form_for @q do |f| %> <%= f.search_field :title_cont %> <% end %> <%= sort_link(@q, :published_at) %> ``` ## Documentation **[activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/)**: [getting started](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/getting-started/), [authorization](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/getting-started/authorization/), [predicates](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/getting-started/search-matches/), [upgrading](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/getting-started/upgrading/) and more. The site is built from the Markdown under [`docs/`](docs/). ## Getting help and contributing * Questions belong in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/discussions). * Reproducible bugs belong in [Issues](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/issues). Read the [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; a failing test is the best bug report. * Report security vulnerabilities privately, through GitHub [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/security/advisories/new) or the [Tidelift security contact](https://tidelift.com/security). See the [Security Policy](.github/SECURITY.md) for supported versions. Ransack is maintained by volunteers. If it is useful to you, please consider supporting us via [Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/ransack), or through the [Tidelift Subscription](https://tidelift.com/subscription/pkg/rubygems-ransack?utm_source=rubygems-ransack&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=enterprise&utm_term=repo) for commercial support. ## Contributors Ransack is maintained by [Sean Carroll](https://github.com/scarroll32), [Deivid Rodriguez](https://github.com/deivid-rodriguez), [Greg Molnar](https://github.com/gregmolnar) and [a great group of contributors](https://github.com/activerecord-hackery/ransack/graphs/contributors). It was created by [Ernie Miller](http://twitter.com/erniemiller). See [Community and support](https://activerecord-hackery.github.io/ransack/project/community/) for the full list.
